name: South Ridge

waypoints.name: Boston Basin Trailhead
waypoints.directions: Follow Cascade River Road (Forest Road 15) to its end at the Boston Basin trailhead, an unsigned pullout at about 3,300 feet, roughly 21.7 miles from Marblemount and directly across from Johannesburg Mountain. Park at the small roadside pullout. Register and pick up your permit through Marblemount before heading up.

waypoints.name: Boston Basin
waypoints.directions: Walk the old Diamond Mine roadbed about three quarters of a mile to a mile, then turn sharp right onto the steep climbers' trail. It switchbacks up through forest across four small creeks to treeline and the low camps around 5,300 ft, then continues up open slabs and tundra on the skier's right of Boston Creek to high camp near 6,200 to 6,400 ft.

waypoints.name: Base of south ridge
waypoints.directions: Leave the trail and make a rising traverse northwest near the 6,200 ft contour beneath Forbidden Peak's south spur, crossing a prominent rock rib below the cliffs. Gain the Taboo Glacier on its climber's left and follow it up to the deep couloir breaking the rock band on the left; cross the bergschrund or moat and scramble about 100 ft of loose class 3-4 to the notch.

waypoints.name: Mount Torment summit
waypoints.directions: Climb an open book angling left off the notch, turn right at its top to a ledge, and take a short second open book to the crest. Pass a steeper tower on sloping, exposed ledges, weave among towers continuing leftward on the southwest face, and finish on sustained fourth and low fifth-class granite to the summit.

approach: Start at the Boston Basin Trailhead (end of Cascade River Road/FR-15). The unmaintained but well-beaten climbers' trail switchbacks steeply up through forest and traverses west, crossing a couple of small creeks (reliable water), to reach the meadows of Boston Basin in roughly 1.5-3.5 hours depending on pace and pack weight. Established low camps sit around 5,300 ft on the basin's tundra benches; from there, continue climbing skier's-right of Boston Creek (a good water source until it's dry/frozen) up open slabs and tundra to the upper high camp near 6,400-6,600 ft, below Sharkfin Tower and Forbidden Peak's south spur. From high camp, do a rising traverse northwest at roughly the 6,200 ft contour, staying beneath Forbidden's south spur, cross a prominent rock rib below the cliffs, and continue toward the toe of the Taboo Glacier. Gain the glacier on its left (climber's left) side and follow it up until a deep gully/couloir breaks through the rock band on the left; a bergschrund or moat typically has to be negotiated here and has been the site of a fatal accident, so treat the crossing seriously, especially early season when it's snow-bridged or late season when it's wide open. Scramble up the gully (class 3-4, loose in spots — helmet recommended) to the South Ridge notch/South Col, about an hour above high camp. Expect firm snow or glacier ice on the approach slopes early in the season (crampons/axe useful) and a short glacier crossing that warrants basic crevasse-rescue readiness even though it is generally low-angle and short.
